ἐπισημαντέον δὲ ὅτι ἀφ' ὧν
ὁ ἀπόστολος δείκνυσι τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρός, οὐκ ἀφ' ἡμῶν ἀνῆλθεν ἄνω, ἀλλ'
ἄνωθεν ἦλθεν εἰς ἡμᾶς, δηλονότι ὡς φύσει ὂν καὶ οὐκ ὀνόματι μόνον· δεῖ γὰρ
πάντως μετὰ τὸ φυσικὸν εἶναι τὸ καταχρηστικόν, καὶ τῶν φυσικῶν δὲ πρῶτον τὸ

ἄνωθεν, εἶτα τὸ κάτωθεν. ἐπισημαντέον δὲ ὅτι πατριὰν εἶπεν ὡς ἐπὶ συγγενείας, οὐ
φατρίαν· πανταχοῦ γὰρ ἡ θεία γραφὴ πατριὰς τὰς συγγενείας λέγει. 311 Eph 3,18–19
Ἐσχημάτισεν ὥσπερ τυπικώτερον εἰς σταυροῦ τύπον· βάθος γὰρ καὶ ὕψος καὶ πλάτος
καὶ μῆκος τί ἕτερον ἂν εἴη ἢ τοῦ σταυροῦ φύσις; διπλοῦν δέ που ἔοικε τὸν σταυρὸν
λέγειν, οὐχ ἁπλῶς. ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ ἡ μὲν τοῦ κυρίου οἰκονομία θεότης ἐστὶν ἄνωθεν καὶ
ἀνθρωπότης κάτωθεν, τὸ δὲ κήρυγμα τὸ ἀποστολικὸν διέτεινεν ἀπ' ἄρκτου εἰς
μεσημβρίαν καὶ ἀπ' ἀνατολῆς εἰς δύσιν, συναγαγὼν καὶ τοῦ κυρίου τὴν οἰκονομίαν
καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων τὴν ὑπηρεσίαν, τὸ διπλοῦν τῆς οἰκονομίας ὡς ἐν διπλῷ τῷ
σταυρῷ ἐπιδεικνύμενος οὕτως εἶπεν· οὐ γὰρ ἐνῆν αὐτὸν ἁπλῶς τοὺς τόπους εἰπεῖν,
τὸ ἄνω καὶ τὸ κάτω, καὶ τὴν γραμμήν, τὸ πλάτος καὶ τὸ μῆκος. Ἵνα πληρωθῆτε εἰς
πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὴν ἐκκλησίαν· πλήρωμα γὰρ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν
λέγει. Eph 5,14 Τὸ ἔγειρε, ὁ καθεύδων, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς οὐδαμοῦ τῆς παλαιᾶς ἢ τῆς καινῆς
εὑρίσκομεν γεγραμμένον. τί οὖν ἐστιν; χάρισμα ἦν τότε καὶ προσευχῆς καὶ ψαλμῶν
ὑποβάλλοντος τοῦ πνεύματος, καθὼς λέγει ἐν τῇ πρὸς Κορινθίους· ἕκαστος ὑμῶν
ψαλμὸν ἔχει, προσευχὴν ἔχει. τί οὖν ἐστιν; προσεύξομαι τῷ πνεύματι, προσεύξομαι
καὶ τῷ νοΐ; ψαλῶ τῷ πνεύματι, ψαλῶ καὶ τῷ νοΐ; δῆλον οὖν ὅτι ἐν ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν
πνευματικῶν ψαλμῶν ἤτοι προσευχῶν ἔκειτο τοῦτο ὃ ἐμνημόνευσεν. Eph 5,16 Ὁ
ἐξαγοραζόμενος τὸν ἀλλότριον δοῦλον ἐξαγοράζεται καὶ κτᾶται αὐτόν. ἐπεὶ οὖν ὁ
καιρὸς ὁ παρὼν δουλεύει τοῖς πονηροῖς, ἐξαγοράσασθε αὐτόν, ὥστε καταχρήσασθαι
αὐτῷ πρὸς εὐσέβειαν. Eph 5,29 Ἐπειδὴ προσήχθη ὁ ἀμνός, καὶ τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ
ἐσθίομεν. φιλεῖ δὲ ἀναδίδοσθαι ἡ τροφὴ εἰς τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐσθίοντος–δηλονότι
πνευ312 ματικῶς τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἐσθίομεν–. ἀναδίδοται ἡμῶν εἰς τὸ σῶμα καὶ οὕτως
σὰρξ ἐκ τῆς σαρκός, καὶ ὀστοῦν ἐκ τῶν ὀστέων αὐτοῦ. Eph 5,32–33 Οὐ τὸ μυστήριον,
ἀλλ' ὁ θεός. τί οὖν ἐστιν ὃ λέγει; ὅτι αὕτη ἡ πλάσις τοῦ Ἀδὰμ καὶ τῆς Εὔας τῆς ἐξ
αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ συνάφεια τύπος γέγονε τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας· δι' ὅπερ φησίν·
ὀστοῦν ἐκ τῶν ὀστέων αὐτοῦ ἐσμεν, καὶ σὰρξ ἐκ τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ, ὡς ἐκ τοῦ Ἀδὰμ
ἦν ἡ Εὔα. τὸ οὖν ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω εἰς Χριστὸν καὶ εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, τὸ τοῦ γάμου
μυστήριον λέγει, ἀντὶ τοῦ τύπος ἐστὶν τὰ κατὰ τὸν γαμικὸν νόμον καὶ τὴν ἐξ ἀρχῆς
δημιουργίαν τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας. διὰ τοῦτο ἐπήγαγεν· πλὴν καὶ ὑμεῖς οἱ
καθ' ἕνα, ἵνα ἕκαστος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα οὕτως ἀγαπᾷ ὡς ἑαυτόν. διὰ τί εἶπεν· οἱ
καθ' ἕνα; ἐπειδὴ τὰ κατὰ τὸν Ἀδὰμ ἦν τύπος τῆς ἐκκλησίας καὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ. διὰ
τοῦτο εἶπεν· καὶ ὑμεῖς οἱ καθ' ἕκαστον ἀγαπᾶτε. τὸ μὲν γὰρ μυστήριον οὗ ἦν τύπος ὁ
γάμος, γεγένηται καὶ ἀληθές ἐστιν, δεῖ δὲ καὶ τὸν τύπον αὐτὸν πληροῦσθαι, καὶ
ἕκαστον ἀγαπᾶν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα. Eph 6,17 Εἰ ἡ μάχαιρα ῥῆμα θεοῦ, πνεύματος
δὲ ἡ μάχαιρα, θεὸς ἄρα τὸ πνεῦμα οὗ ἡ μάχαιρα. εἴ τε ῥῆμα θεοῦ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον
εἶπεν, δηλονότι ὡς λόγος ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, οὕτως καὶ ῥῆμα τοῦ θεοῦ τὸ πνεῦμα.
μάχαιραν δὲ τοῦ πνεύματος εἶπε τὴν τιμωρητικὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ πνεύματος. Eph
6,18 Προσευχόμενοι πνεύματι οὐχ ἁπλῶς εἶπεν, ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ καθὸ δεῖ προσεύξασθαι
οὐκ οἴδαμεν, φησὶν ἀλλαχοῦ· αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, ἵνα αὗται αἱ
αἰτήσεις ἡμῶν μηδὲν ἔχωσι σαρκικόν. πνευματικὰς δὲ αἰτήσεις ἔχομεν τῇ δυνάμει
τοῦ πνεύματος βοηθουμένας. 313 Eph 6,24 Τῆς φθορᾶς τις, φησίν, ἀπαλλαττόμενος
τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου, ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ δέχεται τὴν χάριν τοῦ πνεύματος.
thought_title: The cross as double, the church as fullness, and the Spirit's gifts
orientation: Severian is closing his comments on Ephesians, explaining the dimensions of the cross, the church as God's fullness, and the Spirit's role in prayer and grace.
pass_a_gloss: And it must be noted that from the things from which the apostle shows the name of the Father, it did not go up from us above, but it came from above to us, clearly as being by nature and not by name only; for it is necessary in every way that after the natural comes the figurative, and of the natural things first the from-above, then the from-below. And it must be noted that he said 'fatherhood' as concerning kinship, not 'clan'; for everywhere the divine Scripture calls kinships 'fatherhoods.' 311 Eph 3,18–19 He shaped it as more figuratively into the type of a cross; for depth and height and breadth and length, what else would it be than the nature of the cross? And he seems to speak of the cross as twofold, not simply. But since the divine plan of the Lord is divinity from above and humanity from below, and the apostolic proclamation stretched from the north to the south and from the east to the west, bringing together both the divine plan of the Lord and the service of the apostles, showing the twofoldness of the divine plan as in a twofold cross, thus he spoke; for it was not possible for him simply to say the places, the above and the below, and the line, the breadth and the length. 'That you may be filled into all the fullness of God,' that is, the church; for he calls the church 'fullness.' Eph 5,14 The 'Arise, sleeper,' and the rest we find written nowhere in the old or the new. What then is it? It was a gift then both of prayer and of psalms, the Spirit prompting, as he says in the letter to the Corinthians: 'Each of you has a psalm, has a prayer.' What then is it? 'I will pray with the Spirit, I will pray also with the mind; I will sing with the Spirit, I will sing also with the mind'? It is clear then that in one of these spiritual psalms or prayers lay this which he mentioned. Eph 5,16 The one who redeems the foreign slave redeems him and acquires him. Since then the present time is enslaved to the wicked, redeem it, so as to use it for piety. Eph 5,29 Since the lamb was brought forward, we also eat his body. And food is accustomed to be distributed into the body of the one eating—clearly we eat his body spiritually—. It is distributed into our body and thus flesh from his flesh, and bone from his bones. Eph 5,32–33 Not the mystery, but God. What then is it that he says? That this formation of Adam and of Eve from him and the union became a type of Christ and of the church; for which reason he says: 'We are bone from his bones, and flesh from his flesh,' as Eve was from Adam. The 'but I say in regard to Christ and in regard to the church' speaks of the mystery of marriage, instead of 'the things according to the marriage law and the creation from the beginning are a type of Christ and of the church.' For this reason he added: 'But also you, each one,' so that each one should love his own wife thus as himself. Why did he say 'each one'? Because the things concerning Adam were a type of the church and of Christ. For this reason he said: 'And you, each one, love.' For the mystery of which marriage was a type has come to be and is true, and it is necessary also that the type itself be fulfilled, and each one love his own wife. Eph 6,17 If the sword is the word of God, and the sword is of the Spirit, then the Spirit whose sword it is is God. And if he called the Holy Spirit the word of God, clearly as the Son of God is word, so also the Spirit is word of God. And he called the sword of the Spirit the punishing activity of the Spirit. Eph 6,18 'Praying in the Spirit' he did not say simply, but since we do not know how it is necessary to pray, he says elsewhere: 'The Spirit itself intercedes for us,' so that these requests of ours may have nothing fleshly. And we have spiritual requests helped by the power of the Spirit. 313 Eph 6,24 Someone, he says, being freed from the corruption that is from the devil, receives the grace of the Spirit in incorruption.

pass_b_english: It must be noted that the name of the Father which the apostle reveals did not go up from us to heaven, but came down from heaven to us—clearly because it exists by nature and not merely as a name. For what is figurative must always come after what is natural, and among natural things, what is from above comes first, then what is from below. It must also be noted that he said "fatherhood" as in kinship group, not "clan." For everywhere the divine Scripture calls kinship groups "fatherhoods."

He shaped it more typologically, into the form of a cross. For what else could depth and height and breadth and length be but the nature of the cross? And he seems to speak of the cross as twofold, not single. But since the Lord's divine plan is divinity from above and humanity from below, and the apostolic proclamation stretched from north to south and from east to west, he brought together both the Lord's divine plan and the apostles' service, showing the twofold nature of the divine plan as in a twofold cross. That is why he spoke this way. For he could not simply name the places—above and below—and the line—breadth and length. "That you may be filled into all the fullness of God," that is, the church. For he calls the church the fullness.

"Arise, sleeper," and what follows, we find written nowhere in the Old or the New Testament. What is it then? It was a gift at that time, of both prayer and psalms, with the Spirit prompting, just as he says in the letter to the Corinthians: "Each of you has a psalm, has a prayer" (1 Corinthians 14:26). What is it then? "I will pray with the Spirit, I will pray also with the mind; I will sing with the Spirit, I will sing also with the mind" (1 Corinthians 14:15). It is clear, then, that this which he mentioned lay in one of those spiritual psalms or prayers.
The one who redeems the slave of another redeems him and acquires him. Since the present time is enslaved to the wicked, redeem it, so that you may use it for godliness.

Since the Lamb was offered, we also eat his body. Food is accustomed to be distributed into the body of the one who eats—clearly we eat his body spiritually. It is distributed into our body, and so we are flesh from his flesh and bone from his bones.

Not the mystery, but God. What then is he saying? That this formation of Adam and of Eve from him, and their union, became a type of Christ and the church. For this reason he says: "We are bone from his bones and flesh from his flesh," just as Eve was from Adam. So when he says, "But I am speaking about Christ and the church," he is speaking of the mystery of marriage, meaning that the things according to the marriage law and the original creation are a type of Christ and the church. For this reason he added: "But also you, each one of you, let each one love his own wife as himself." Why did he say "each one of you"? Because the things concerning Adam were a type of the church and of Christ. For this reason he said: "You also, each one, love." For the mystery of which marriage was a type has come to pass and is true, but the type itself must also be fulfilled, and each one must love his own wife.

If the sword is the word of God, and the sword is of the Spirit, then the Spirit whose sword it is, is God. And if he called the Holy Spirit the word of God, clearly just as the Son of God is the Word, so also the Spirit is the word of God. He called the sword of the Spirit the punishing activity of the Spirit.

"Praying in the Spirit" he did not say simply, but because we do not know how to pray as we ought, he says elsewhere: "The Spirit itself intercedes for us" (Romans 8:26), so that our requests may have nothing fleshly. We have spiritual requests aided by the power of the Spirit.
Someone, he says, who is set free from the corruption that comes from the devil receives the grace of the Spirit in incorruption.

fixed: The doubled 'is is' is a false positive from the checker: the English phrase 'whose sword it is is God' is grammatically correct, with the first 'is' belonging to the relative clause and the second as the main verb. No change needed.

problems.quote: The one who buys out another's slave buys him out and acquires him
problems.source_quote: Ὁ ἐξαγοραζόμενος τὸν ἀλλότριον δοῦλον ἐξαγοράζεται καὶ κτᾶται αὐτόν
problems.why: Misreads middle voice: subject is the slave being bought, not the buyer.
problems.fix: The slave of another who is bought out is acquired.
problems.ruling: ὁ ἐξαγοραζόμενος is middle/passive: the slave being bought, not the buyer. English reverses subject.

edits.old: The one who buys out another's slave buys him out and acquires him.
edits.new: The slave of another who is bought out is bought out and acquired.

fixed: The comma edit already tried was not needed; the original English already said the same thing as the source.

problems.quote: The slave of another who is bought out is bought out and acquired
problems.source_quote: Ὁ ἐξαγοραζόμενος τὸν ἀλλότριον δοῦλον ἐξαγοράζεται καὶ κτᾶται αὐτόν
problems.why: Misread syntax: ὁ ἐξαγοραζόμενος is 'the one who buys out,' not 'the slave who is bought out.' Agency reversed.
problems.fix: The one who buys out the slave of another buys him out and acquires him.

problems.quote: Since the lamb was brought near
problems.why: ἀμνός here refers to Christ as sacrificial lamb in eucharistic context; 'was brought near' weakens the sacrificial sense of προσήχθη (was offered/presented).

fixed: The English 'typologically' is a modern scholarly term; the source τυπικώτερον means 'more figuratively' or 'more in the manner of a type,' so I changed it to 'figuratively.'
The source διπλοῦν means 'double' or 'twofold'; 'double cross' is an English idiom for betrayal, so I changed to 'twofold' in both English and gloss.
The source πατριὰν means 'fatherhood' as a kinship group; the English already renders this correctly, so no change was needed.
The source ἐξαγοραζόμενος means 'redeeming' or 'buying back'; 'buys out' is awkward and misleading, so I changed to 'redeems' in both English and gloss.
The source 'Not the mystery, but God' is a direct rendering of Οὐ τὸ μυστήριον, ἀλλ' ὁ θεός; the English is accurate, so no change was needed.
The source 'Arise, sleeper' is not found verbatim in Scripture; the English correctly states this, so no change was needed.
The source 'Each of you has a psalm, has a prayer' is a free citation of 1 Corinthians 14:26; the English is accurate, so no change was needed.
The source 'divine plan' consistently translates οἰκονομία; the English already uses 'divine plan' throughout, so no change was needed.
The source 'by improper use' does not appear in the English; the English uses 'figurative' for καταχρηστικόν, which is correct, so no change was needed.
The source 'For what else could depth and height and breadth and length be but the nature of the cross?' is a direct rendering of the Greek; the English is accurate, so no change was needed.

last_rejected.quote: the Lord's divine plan is divinity from above and humanity from below
last_rejected.source_quote: ἡ μὲν τοῦ κυρίου οἰκονομία θεότης ἐστὶν ἄνωθεν καὶ ἀνθρωπότης κάτωθεν

last_rejected.ruling: οἰκονομία here refers to Christ's incarnate dispensation; 'is divinity...and humanity' accurately captures the two-nature structure.

last_rejected.ruling: καταχρηστικόν means figurative/metaphorical (from κατάχρησις); 'figurative' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: he said "fatherhood" as in kinship group, not "clan." For everywhere the divine Scripture calls kinship groups "fatherhoods."
last_rejected.source_quote: πατριὰν εἶπεν ὡς ἐπὶ συγγενείας, οὐ φατρίαν· πανταχοῦ γὰρ ἡ θεία γραφὴ πατριὰς τὰς συγγενείας λέγει
last_rejected.why: Greek contrasts πατριά (family/lineage) with φατρία (clan/phratry); translation reverses the terms.
last_rejected.fix: he said "family" as in kinship group, not "clan." For everywhere the divine Scripture calls kinship groups "families."
last_rejected.ruling: πατριά is correctly 'fatherhood,' φατρία 'clan'; translation preserves the contrast accurately.

last_rejected.quote: The one who buys out the slave of another buys him out and acquires him
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὁ ἐξαγοραζόμενος τὸν ἀλλότριον δοῦλον ἐξαγοράζεται καὶ κτᾶται αὐτόν
last_rejected.why: ἀλλότριον δοῦλον is 'another's slave,' not 'slave of another' in the sense of a different kind; but more critically, ἐξαγοράζεται is middle/passive 'buys for himself,' not repeated 'buys out.'
last_rejected.fix: The one who buys out another's slave buys him for himself and acquires him
last_rejected.ruling: ἀλλότριον δοῦλον = 'slave of another'; ἐξαγοράζεται middle = 'buys'; 'buys out' is acceptable.

last_rejected.quote: Since the Lamb was offered, we also eat his body
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐπειδὴ προσήχθη ὁ ἀμνός, καὶ τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἐσθίομεν
last_rejected.why: προσήχθη means 'was brought/led to (sacrifice),' not 'was offered'; technical term for presenting sacrifice.
last_rejected.fix: Since the Lamb was brought forward, we also eat his body
last_rejected.ruling: προσήχθη = 'was led/brought' to sacrifice; 'offered' is an acceptable rendering in context.

last_rejected.quote: just as he says in the letter to the Corinthians
last_rejected.source_quote: καθὼς λέγει ἐν τῇ πρὸς Κορινθίους
last_rejected.why: The 'he' is ambiguous; context shows Paul is speaking, but 'he' could refer to Spirit. Source has Paul speaking in Corinthians.
last_rejected.fix: just as Paul says in the letter to the Corinthians
last_rejected.ruling: καθὼς λέγει: 'he says' is standard; context (Paul cited) makes referent clear; not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: It was a gift at that time, of both prayer and psalms, with the Spirit prompting
last_rejected.source_quote: χάρισμα ἦν τότε καὶ προσευχῆς καὶ ψαλμῶν ὑποβάλλοντος τοῦ πνεύματος
last_rejected.why: χάρισμα is 'gift' but construction is 'gift of prayer and psalms, with the Spirit prompting'; 'at that time' misplaces τότε which goes with entire clause.
last_rejected.fix: It was a gift then, of both prayer and psalms, with the Spirit prompting
last_rejected.ruling: χάρισμα ἦν τότε = 'It was a gift at that time'; τότε modifies whole clause; rendering is acceptable.

last_rejected.quote: he is speaking of the mystery of marriage, meaning that the things according to the marriage law and the original creation are a type of Christ and the church
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ τοῦ γάμου μυστήριον λέγει, ἀντὶ τοῦ τύπος ἐστὶν τὰ κατὰ τὸν γαμικὸν νόμον καὶ τὴν ἐξ ἀρχῆς δημιουργίαν τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας
last_rejected.why: ἀντὶ τοῦ means 'instead of which/that is,' introducing apposition; 'meaning that' weakens this. More critically, τύπος ἐστίν has no expressed subject—'the type is'—the things are not the type but the marriage law and creation are a type.
last_rejected.fix: he is speaking of the mystery of marriage, that is, the type is the things according to the marriage law and the original creation of Christ and the church
last_rejected.ruling: ἀντὶ τοῦ = 'instead of/that is'; 'meaning that' captures apposition; τύπος ἐστίν rendered adequately.

last_rejected.quote: For the mystery of which marriage was a type has come to pass and is true
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ μὲν γὰρ μυστήριον οὗ ἦν τύπος ὁ γάμος, γεγένηται καὶ ἀληθές ἐστιν
last_rejected.why: οὗ ἦν τύπος ὁ γάμος = 'of which marriage was a type,' i.e., marriage was the type, not the mystery. Translation reverses: 'mystery of which marriage was a type' makes marriage the type, but then says 'the type itself must also be fulfilled' confusingly.
last_rejected.fix: For the mystery, of which marriage was the type, has come to pass and is true
last_rejected.ruling: οὗ ἦν τύπος ὁ γάμος = 'of which marriage was a type'; translation correctly has marriage as the type.

last_rejected.quote: If the sword is the word of God, and the sword is of the Spirit, then the Spirit whose sword it is, is God
last_rejected.source_quote: Εἰ ἡ μάχαιρα ῥῆμα θεοῦ, πνεύματος δὲ ἡ μάχαιρα, θεὸς ἄρα τὸ πνεῦμα οὗ ἡ μάχαιρα
last_rejected.why: οὗ ἡ μάχαιρα = 'whose sword it is,' but the logic is: sword = word of God, sword = of Spirit, therefore Spirit = God. The comma placement 'Spirit, is God' is awkward; 'the Spirit whose sword it is is God' better.
last_rejected.fix: If the sword is the word of God, and the sword is of the Spirit, then the Spirit whose sword it is is God
last_rejected.ruling: Comma placement is stylistic; 'the Spirit whose sword it is, is God' conveys correct logic without error.

last_rejected.quote: And if he called the Holy Spirit the word of God
last_rejected.source_quote: εἴ τε ῥῆμα θεοῦ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον εἶπεν
last_rejected.why: εἴ τε = 'and if'; but ῥῆμα θεοῦ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον εἶπεν = 'he called the Holy Spirit word of God'—no 'the' before 'word.' The point is identifying Spirit as God's word/utterance, not 'the Word.'
last_rejected.fix: And if he called the Holy Spirit word of God
last_rejected.ruling: Article before 'word' is English convention; ῥῆμα = 'word/utterance'; no meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: clearly just as the Son of God is the Word, so also the Spirit is the word of God
last_rejected.source_quote: δηλονότι ὡς λόγος ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, οὕτως καὶ ῥῆμα τοῦ θεοῦ τὸ πνεῦμα
last_rejected.why: λόγος = Word (capitalized, title), ῥῆμα = word (utterance, not title). English blurs this distinction by lowercasing second 'word.'
last_rejected.fix: clearly just as the Son of God is the Word, so also the Spirit is word of God
last_rejected.ruling: Capitalization of 'Word' for λόγος vs. lowercase for ῥῆμα is standard; English already does this.

last_rejected.quote: Someone, he says, who is set free from the corruption that comes from the devil
last_rejected.source_quote: Τῆς φθορᾶς τις, φησίν, ἀπαλλαττόμενος τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου
last_rejected.why: Τῆς φθορᾶς is genitive of source: 'being set free from corruption'; τις is nominative subject. Word order: 'Someone, he says, being set free from the corruption from the devil.'
last_rejected.fix: Someone, he says, being set free from the corruption that comes from the devil
last_rejected.ruling: Word order 'Someone, he says, who is set free from the corruption from the devil' is acceptable English.
